AK-2025-SCR10.aiSummary: This resolution would let lawmakers set aside some state legislative rules so they can consider House Bill 36. That bill is about placing foster children in psychiatric hospitals, caring for children in state custody who are placed in care facilities outside Alaska, and changing a court procedure rule for children in need of aid. It was passed by the legislature.

AK-2025-HCR9.aiSummary: The resolution would honor the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence and the founding of the United States. It would encourage people, schools, civic groups, and businesses in Alaska to take part in events that reflect on U.S. history and core ideals. It would also encourage schools to strengthen civics education so students learn about civic participation, federalism, and self-government.

AK-2025-HB36.aiSummary: The bill updates rules for treatment foster homes and for children in state custody who need psychiatric care. It lets the state place some children in a hospital or residential psychiatric treatment center for short-term mental health care, with court review and notice to the child, family, and other parties. It also changes related duties for the Department of Family and Community Services and a court rule, and it became law with an effective date the same as passage.

AK-2025-HB3002.title: An Act relating to the elimination of income taxes on pass-through entities.
AK-2025-HB3002.aiSummary: The bill would end Alaska’s income tax on pass-through businesses, which are businesses that pass profits through to the owners’ personal taxes. It would repeal the current law on January 1, 2028.

AK-2025-HB184.aiSummary: This law lets the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority help finance new workforce housing projects with three or more homes. It also adds certain housing assets of the authority to a required exemption from city property taxes. The law took effect on September 16, 2026.
